subject: Re: [AMBER] how find Es from mdout to estimate vertical energy gap

messages.author: Vaibhav Dixit
messages.body:
Dear All,
I'm now able to estimate E differences between the two-states which are
very much in the expected range of 0.7 eV.
I will try the pmemd.MPI option for SP Es, but this choice raises another
query for which I can't quickly find the most updated answer.
There were some very old discussions for differences in sander and pmemd
based E-estimates (here <
http://ambermd.org/Questions/mail/308.html
>).
Can someone please update me what is expected with Amber18 and newer
versions?
Are the sander and pmemd Es expected to be highly similar and thus one can
ignore whether these E are derived from sander, pmemd (serial, MPI) or even
cpptraj as Adrian suggested to try out?
Or one should use a consistent/identical protocol for estimating Es
especially when one wants to extract/compare differences between two
trajectories or states (and when the expect avg, variance, std are not
known)?
Looking forward to receiving valuable suggestions and guidance from the
list.
Thank you all (and Adrian for valuable suggestions earlier).
Best regards

> >>> identical."
> >>>
> >>> If they are identical, then you will get the EXACT same answer for the
> >>> same geometry for both states, which is not what you want, agree ?
> >>>
> >>>
> >>> Second: imin=5 does not give you EKtot, etc because there is NO
> velocity
> >>> information in your dynamics file, just coordinates, so the only thing
> >>> you can compute is the potential energy.
> >>>
> >>> Third, I would do imin=5 with your two prmtops.
> >>>
> >>> There is a chance that your mdout and mdcrd files are offset, maybe by
> >>> just one frame, so you could get in trouble.
> >>>
> >>> Just run MD with prmtop_1, save mdcrd, and do TWO imin=5 runs, one with
> >>> prmtop_1 and one with prmtop_2
> >>>
> >>> Makes sense ?
> >>>
